column1: # A bare number cannot be verified. "0.19" appears inside a thousand NLL values;
# "6.6" appears inside "PPL 26.655". A figure is only checkable if we also say
# WHAT QUANTITY it is. Each row therefore declares the unit that must sit
# adjacent to the number and the keywords that must appear on the same line (or
# in the filename) for a hit to count.
#   id            short slug, used in output
#   value         the number as published (printed precision sets the tolerance)
#   unit          unit that must immediately follow the number; "-" for none
#   keywords      pipe-separated; at least one must appear on the matching line
#                 or in the matching file's name
#   description   what the figure actually claims
# Tolerance is derived from printed precision: 5.140 admits [5.1395, 5.1405);
# 0.19 admits [0.185, 0.195). Rounding is legitimate, drift is not.
